claims.statement: The main backend integrates with the AI runtime over HTTP using `AI_RUNTIME_URL` defaulting to `http://localhost:8000`; decision-memory chat and greeting handlers call `/api/v1/chat`, `/api/v1/chat/stream`, and `/api/v1/greeting`, while the AI runtime mounts its router under `/api/v1` and exposes a separate `/health` endpoint.

Decision-memory chat is a stateful backend-to-AI-runtime contract: before calling the runtime the backend verifies session ownership, persists the new user message, rebuilds the conversation from stored user and assistant messages, derives `allowed_comparison_ids` from prior assistant reasoning payloads, and after a successful response persists the assistant message with the full runtime envelope stored in `ReasoningGraph`.

Streaming chat is proxied as Server-Sent Events from the AI runtime: the runtime emits `token`, optional decision events, `ui_operation`, `envelope`, and `done`, while the backend forwards SSE blocks to the client, reconstructs the final assistant payload from stream events, and persists the assistant message at stream completion or emits an SSE `error` if persistence fails.

Decision-memory session routes intentionally support anonymous as well as authenticated callers: `OptionalAuth` ignores missing or invalid bearer tokens, anonymous identity is taken from `X-Anonymous-ID`, create and list operations require either a user ID or anonymous ID, session ownership checks compare against whichever identity channel is present, and `UpdateSession` requires `X-Client-Timestamp` for conflict handling.

Greeting generation is a soft dependency on the AI runtime and the LLM provider: the backend collects recent user-message facts from the latest session when identity is available and calls `/api/v1/greeting`, but falls back to a local generic greeting on request or response failure, and the AI runtime itself also catches provider failures and returns a local fallback greeting.

The AI runtime uses an OpenAI-compatible provider configured by `openai_api_key`, optional `openai_base_url`, and `model`; it retries chat completions up to three times with exponential backoff on OpenAI connection, rate-limit, and API errors, and uses strict JSON-schema output for greeting drafts.

The AI runtime has an internal reverse dependency on the main backend through `ToolProxy`, using `backend_url` defaulting to `http://localhost:18080` to call `GET /api/v1/products` and `GET /api/v1/products/{product_id}/offer-comparison` with a 10 second timeout; HTTP failures are surfaced from the chat endpoint as `502 catalog unavailable`.

Google OAuth is optional and only enabled when both `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` are present; the backend starts the flow by setting an HTTP-only `shopwise_oauth_state` cookie and redirecting to Google, exchanges the callback code using scopes `openid`, `email`, and `profile`, fetches user info from `https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/userinfo`, and finally redirects the browser to `${WEB_APP_URL}/auth/callback` with access and refresh tokens in the query string.

Resume-session notifications are architected behind a `NotificationProvider` abstraction, but the currently wired Zalo provider is still a mock: bootstrap injects a Zalo provider wrapped in `RetryableProvider`, the provider only simulates latency and returns `StatusAccepted`, and comments note that a real implementation would call the Zalo OA API and classify transient versus permanent failures.

The resume-session flow preserves single-use token semantics in the backend rather than in the notification transport: generating a token revokes prior unconsumed tokens for the session, stores only a SHA-256 hash of the issued JWT, resuming validates the token and rejects revoked, consumed, expired, or mismatched records, marks the token consumed, and `GET /api/v1/session/resume` hashes client IP plus user agent as a context signal for auditing.

Phong Vu integrations are optional and feature-flagged by `PHONGVU_CONNECTOR_ENABLED`: the main backend wires a Phong Vu offer refresher into order services, and the worker only registers the Phong Vu accessory sync handler, 6 hour schedule, and initial unique sync task when the flag is enabled.

The worker’s Phong Vu accessory sync integration fetches a fixed set of Phong Vu category URLs, normalizes the fetched products into accessory sync records, and runs through Redis-backed Asynq scheduling infrastructure.

Postgres and Redis are hard startup dependencies for both the main backend and worker: configuration loading requires `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, and `JWT_SECRET`; the database layer opens Postgres, creates the `vector` extension, auto-migrates shared models, and creates pgvector HNSW indexes; Redis connectivity is validated with `PING` and is also used for Asynq job infrastructure.

Swagger is a debug-only runtime surface in the main backend: `/swagger/*any` is registered only when `GIN_MODE` is debug, while repository contract tests load `services/main-backend/docs/swagger.yaml` and assert it remains a superset of the onboarding OpenAPI contract under `specs/002-get-started-onboarding/contracts/openapi.yaml`.

Cloudflare web deployment depends on an env-backed backend URL binding: `packages/infra/alchemy.run.ts` loads env files, requires `VITE_SERVER_URL`, and passes it as a binding to the Cloudflare `Vite` deployment helper, so deployment fails fast if the browser app’s backend base URL is unset.
